FUZZ_DISSECTORS="ip"
FUZZ_IP_PROTO_DISSECTORS="udp ospf"
FUZZ_TCP_PORT_DISSECTORS="bgp"
FUZZ_UDP_PORT_DISSECTORS="dns bootp"
FUZZ_MEDIA_TYPE_DISSECTORS="json"
generate_fuzzer()
{
  local fuzzer_target="$1" fuzzer_cflags="$2" fuzzer_name
  fuzzer_name="fuzzshark_$1"
  $CC $CFLAGS -I $SRC/wireshark/ `pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0`       $SRC/wireshark/tools/oss-fuzzshark.c       -c -o $WORK/${fuzzer_name}.o       $fuzzer_cflags
  $CXX $CXXFLAGS $WORK/${fuzzer_name}.o       -o $OUT/${fuzzer_name}       ${WIRESHARK_FUZZERS_COMMON_FLAGS}
  echo -en "[libfuzzer]\nmax_len = 1024\n" > $OUT/${fuzzer_name}.options
  if [ -d "$SAMPLES_DIR/${fuzzer_target}" ]; then
    zip -j $OUT/${fuzzer_name}_seed_corpus.zip $SAMPLES_DIR/${fuzzer_target}/*/*.bin
  fi
}
export WIRESHARK_INSTALL_PATH="$WORK/install"
mkdir -p "$WIRESHARK_INSTALL_PATH"
SAMPLES_DIR="$WORK/samples"
mkdir -p "$SAMPLES_DIR"
cp -a $SRC/wireshark-fuzzdb/samples/* "$SAMPLES_DIR"
CONFOPTS="--disable-shared --enable-static --without-plugins"
CONFOPTS="$CONFOPTS --without-pcap --without-ssl --without-gnutls"
CONFOPTS="$CONFOPTS --disable-wireshark --disable-tshark --disable-sharkd              --disable-dumpcap --disable-capinfos --disable-captype --disable-randpkt --disable-dftest              --disable-editcap --disable-mergecap --disable-reordercap --disable-text2pcap              --without-extcap          "
sed -i '/AC_WIRESHARK_GCC_FORTIFY_SOURCE_CHECK/d' configure.ac
./autogen.sh
./configure --prefix="$WIRESHARK_INSTALL_PATH" $CONFOPTS --disable-warnings-as-errors
make "-j$(nproc)"
make install
WIRESHARK_FUZZERS_COMMON_FLAGS="-lFuzzingEngine     -L"$WIRESHARK_INSTALL_PATH/lib" -lwireshark -lwiretap -lwsutil     -Wl,-Bstatic `pkg-config --libs glib-2.0` -pthread -lpcre -lgcrypt -lgpg-error -lz -Wl,-Bdynamic"
for dissector in $FUZZ_DISSECTORS; do
  generate_fuzzer "${dissector}" -DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TARGET=\"$dissector\"
done
for dissector in $FUZZ_IP_PROTO_DISSECTORS; do
  generate_fuzzer "ip_proto-${dissector}" "-DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TABLE=\"ip.proto\" -DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TARGET=\"$dissector\""
done
for dissector in $FUZZ_TCP_PORT_DISSECTORS; do
  generate_fuzzer "tcp_port-${dissector}" "-DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TABLE=\"tcp.port\" -DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TARGET=\"$dissector\""
done
for dissector in $FUZZ_UDP_PORT_DISSECTORS; do
  generate_fuzzer "udp_port-${dissector}" "-DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TABLE=\"udp.port\" -DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TARGET=\"$dissector\""
done
for dissector in $FUZZ_MEDIA_TYPE_DISSECTORS; do
  generate_fuzzer "media_type-${dissector}" "-DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TABLE=\"media_type\" -DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TARGET=\"$dissector\""
done

The repo's build.sh here lists: ip; ip_proto udp ospf; tcp_port bgp; udp_port dns bootp; media_type json. Hmm, no ieee80211. But the description says ieee80211. Note: this build.sh might be from an oss-fuzz fork used by ARVO at the time of the vuln commit. Wait — this build.sh IS in the repo (src-vul/build.sh). ARVO tasks build with this. So the fuzzer targets are those listed. How does ieee80211 get reached?

Option A: The "ip" fuzzer — ip dissector on the whole buffer. ieee80211 is not reachable from ip... except? No.

Option B: udp fuzzer (ip.proto table udp). udp → maybe ... no ieee80211.

Option C: dns, bootp, bgp, json... no.

Hmm wait. Actually maybe ieee80211 gets reached via the udp dissector? There is "udp.port" for... no.

Hold on — maybe via the ospf? no.

Hmm, what about bootp (DHCP)? DHCP packets can include... no ieee80211.

Wait, maybe the fuzzer harness with pkt_encap=G_MAXINT16: the top-level dissector. The "ip" fuzzer calls find_dissector("ip") directly. But this build.sh might not be the exact arvo build. Let me check if there's an oss-fuzz build directory inside the repo with a different config... Actually the ARVO task metadata includes checksum. The actual ARVO build for the vulnerable version might use the wireshark repo's own tools/oss-fuzz-build.sh (which is what we saw). Hmm.

But then how does ieee80211 get fuzzed? Let me check the ARVO database knowledge: arvo:1268 — I recall ARVO tasks are from OSS-Fuzz "fixed" bugs. The fuzz target for a wireshark bug in ieee80211 would be fuzzshark_ieee80211. In the actual oss-fuzz wireshark build.sh, FUZZ_DISSECTORS included "ip ieee80211 vlan ip_sec sphinx_...". Hmm, at some point they added ieee80211 to the list. The version in the repo (wireshark 2.3.0, Nov 2016) corresponds to oss-fuzz wireshark build around then.

Actually the description says "ieee80211 code" — the crash location. The crash could be reached through any dissector that calls into ieee80211. Hmm: udp fuzzer? No.

Wait — actually! The top-level dissector for the "ip" fuzzer... no.

Let me reconsider: maybe the vulnerable function is `capture_ieee80211` or the "wlan" conversation tap using `whdr->src/dst` pointing to stack `wlan_hdr_t` in dissect_ieee80211_common. But that requires ieee80211 dissector invoked.

Alternatively, maybe the bug is reached via "bootp"? DHCP option 61? no.

Hmm, alternatively via "dns"? no.

Wait — could ieee80211 be reached from the udp dissector via "udp.port" = ... ? No.

What about via "bgp"? no.

OK here's another thought: maybe the ARVO build.sh differs from what's in the repo — the repo's build.sh IS what ARVO used (they store the vulnerable build). The fuzzers listed are the only ones. But then how would ieee80211 crash? Unless the crash is in code called by one of the listed dissectors, and the description is just approximate ("ieee80211 code").

Hmm, wait — actually, "udp" fuzzer: udp dissector → decodes... udp payload dissected by udp.port table... For unknown ports, calls "data". Hmm no ieee80211.

Actually wait — DHCP (bootp) has option 53 etc. But also there's "bootp.dhcp" — and DHCP packets for WiMAX? Hmm.

Let me think about which of the listed dissectors can reach ieee80211 in Wireshark 2.3: 

- The "wlan" data dissector is reached from... Hmm, "ieee80211" dissector registered in "wtap_encap" table. 

- `ieee80211_radio`? Reached from radiotap. Not from the listed ones.

Hmm, wait. Actually — maybe through the "eth" dissector with a specific ethertype! IEEE 802.11 frames can be encapsulated in Ethernet via "802.11 frames" ethertype 0x890d (802.11 data frames)? Let me check: packet-eth.c might register ETH_PROTO 0x890d → ieee80211_data? Hmm, is there such a thing in 2.3? There's "ethertype 0x890d" = "802.11 data frames" in newer versions I believe.

Alternatively, LLC... no.

Hmm, but actually — maybe I should reconsider the harness. Wait: `whdr.pkt_encap = G_MAXINT16;` — maybe in this Wireshark version, the frame dissector uses pkt_encap to look up the wtap_encap dissector; G_MAXINT16 is unknown, so it falls back to "data". But the FUZZ_DISSECTOR_TARGET "ip" is registered as a postdissector, and postdissectors run after the frame dissector... Hmm no, postdissectors run after the main dissection of the tree; the "ip" handle as postdissector gets called on the frame's tvb? Let me check how register_postdissector works with add_layers... Actually in this harness, the actual dissection is via the frame dissector with pkt_encap=G_MAXINT16 → unknown encap → "data" dissector. Then postdissectors run. Hmm, but then the "ip" postdissector would dissect the whole frame as ip? Postdissectors are called with... hmm, they're called with the full tvb I believe (in packet.c, add_layers / call_all_postdissectors with the full tvb). Actually postdissector call: after dissection completes, for each postdissector, call it with tvb of the frame. So the "ip" fuzzer dissects the input as IP. That matches "FUZZ_DISSECTORS=ip" fuzzing ip directly on raw bytes.

So for the ieee80211 target, the harness would need FUZZ_DISSECTOR_TARGET="ieee80211" and the postdissector would dissect raw bytes as ieee80211! That's how it works: the fuzz target dissector is invoked as a postdissector on the whole frame data. So the ARVO build for this task must have had FUZZ_DISSECTORS including ieee80211. The build.sh in the repo maybe was updated... hmm, but the repo build.sh doesn't list ieee80211.

Wait, let me re-read build.sh: FUZZ_DISSECTORS="ip". Hmm. But this could be the *current* (fixed?) version... no, src-vul is the vulnerable source. Hmm, but build.sh sits outside wireshark/ — it's the oss-fuzz build script snapshot. ARVO uses the oss-fuzz project build.sh at the vulnerable commit time. Since the description mentions ieee80211, maybe the arvo build used a different build.sh... 

Hmm, hold on. Maybe I misread. Let me double check the build.sh content: "FUZZ_DISSECTORS=\"ip\"" — yes. Hmm.

But wait — ARVO tasks for wireshark: each arvo task ID corresponds to an OSS-Fuzz bug. The build.sh used would be from the oss-fuzz repo at the time the vuln was introduced/fixed (2016-2017). Let me check when "ieee80211" was added to FUZZ_DISSECTORS in oss-fuzz wireshark build.sh. I believe the original list was: FUZZ_DISSECTORS="ip ieee80211 vlan ip_sec sphynx..."? Hmm, not sure.

Actually, I recall oss-fuzz wireshark build.sh early version:
```
FUZZ_DISSECTORS="ip"
FUZZ_IP_PROTO_DISSECTORS="udp ospf"
FUZZ_TCP_PORT_DISSECTORS="bgp"
FUZZ_UDP_PORT_DISSECTORS="dns bootp"
FUZZ_MEDIA_TYPE_DISSECTORS="json"
```
That matches exactly what we see! So this build.sh is from oss-fuzz circa 2017. So the ieee80211 dissector isn't directly fuzzed by these targets... but the bug is "in the ieee80211 code". How can these targets reach ieee80211?

Hmm! Maybe via "udp"? Wait — there IS a path: udp → udp.port table... no.

Let me think: which of these dissectors calls ieee80211? Search the codebase for references to ieee80211 handles/registers.

Actually — I remember now! The DHCP dissector (bootp) handles DHCP option 60/61... no. Hmm.

Wait, what about "ip" → "ip.proto" table... no ieee80211.

Hold on, what about the possibility that the crash is in ieee80211 code reached via the **data dissector fallback**? No.

Let me grep for who calls the ieee80211 dissector handle in the tree."}

**"IEEE 802.11 dissector: stack-use-after-return in `dissect_ieee80211_common()`"** hmm.

Actually, you know what — I recall a REAL commit in wireshark: 
commit " ieee80211: Fix stack-use-after-return" — changed:

```c
-  static wlan_hdr_t whdrs[4];
```
NO wait. Hmm, hmm. Actually, let me think about `copy_address_shallow(&whdr->src, &pinfo->dl_src)`. pinfo->dl_src... in dissect_ieee80211_common for DATA frames, at 18086: set_address_tvb(&pinfo->dl_src, ..., tvb, sa_offset). #0 in add_conversation_table_data ... #1 wlan_conversation_packet ... #2 call_all_tap_listeners ... #3 dissect_ieee80211_common ...

Look at 18086-18092: for DATA frames with mesh control... `sa_offset`... but what if the DATA frame's sta address is set via `set_address_tvb(&pinfo->dl_src, wlan_address_type, 6, tvb, sa_offset)` — fine, points into tvb.

BUT — look at line 17442: `station_name = tvb_get_ether_name(tvb, sta_addr_offset)`. Hmm no.

OK — let me look at what `wlan_address_type` is when... hmm irrelevant.

New idea: examine the ACTUAL data dissection path — `dissect_ieee80211_data` — and the amsdu handling (dissect_a_msdu). Let me look at that code; I recall the fix commit for a Wireshark 2.x bug: "ieee80211: fix stack-use-after-scope/return in a-MSDU subframe dissection" — because `dissect_a_msdu` creates a tvb over... let me check.

Let me grep for "a_msdu" or "amsdu" in the file.

I am thinking...: Web access is failing (proxy error). I'll work offline from the source code.

Let me approach this systematically: I need to find where a stack address escapes its function's lifetime in the ieee80211 dissection path reachable from the fuzz targets.

Key insight about ASAN stack-use-after-return detection: it's only reported when ASAN's `detect_stack_use_after_return=1` (which OSS-Fuzz enables by default in its runs, via ASAN_OPTIONS). ARVO reproduces OSS-Fuzz crashes including SUAR.

Since the whdr is static, and used_key is memcpy'd... let me look at the whole dissect_ieee80211_common, particularly:

1. Line 17442: `station_name = tvb_get_ether_name(tvb, sta_addr_offset)` — returns a static buffer? tvb_get_ether_name → ether_to_str? It might return a pointer to a static buffer... fine.

2. Fragment reassembly in data frames: `process_udp_payload`? Let me look at the DATA frame handling code around 18400-18960, especially the fragment_add calls and reassembly — `fragment_add_...` stores tvb data...

Actually! NEW STRONG SUSPICION: **`p_add_proto_data(wmem_file_scope(), pinfo, proto_wlan, IS_DMG_KEY, &isDMG)`** at line ~17166! 

`wmem_file_scope()` — file-scoped memory persists ACROSS packets (across LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput iterations) until file scope is freed. And here it stores `&isDMG` — THE ADDRESS OF A STACK VARIABLE — as the proto data value! The proto data is retrieved later with p_get_proto_data(..., &isDMG_ptr) in the SAME packet though... but since wmem_file_scope data persists across packets, on the NEXT packet, the stored pointer (pointing to the previous packet's stack frame) could be dereferenced!

Let me verify: where is p_get_proto_data(proto_wlan, IS_DMG_KEY) called? If it's called and dereferenced (or compared) — SUAR! And the fix would be to use wmem_packet_scope(). That's EXACTLY the classic bug!

Also `IS_CTRL_GRANT_OR_GRANT_ACK_KEY 2` is another key — let me check where p_add_proto_data is used with that.

Let me grep for p_add_proto_data / p_get_proto_data in packet-ieee80211.c.

If the getter at 14339 is called during dissection of the SAME packet AFTER 17172, the pointer is valid (current stack). Within one fuzz iteration only one packet is dissected, but one packet can contain MULTIPLE ieee80211 frames — e.g., CAPWAP data message contains N ieee80211 frames! Frame 1: dissect_ieee80211_common stores &isDMG (stack address of frame-1 invocation). Frame 2: ... would also call dissect_ieee80211_common first... Hmm.

- 11935: ieee80211_tag_mde? (in some tag dissector — field_data->ftype... i.e., called from within a tagged field dissector: nested IEs!)

message:
I am thinking...: **CONFIRMED mechanism.** In packet-capwap.c line 2713, the CAPWAP dissector calls ieee80211's global `add_tagged_field()` directly — inside its IEEE80211_INFORMATION_ELEMENT (1029) message element parsing. `add_tagged_field` does:

```c
gboolean *p_isDMG = p_get_proto_data(wmem_file_scope(), pinfo, proto_wlan, IS_DMG_KEY);
isDMG = p_isDMG ? *p_isDMG : FALSE;
```

The proto data (file-scoped!) holds `&isDMG` — the address of the `gboolean isDMG` local in `dissect_ieee80211_common`'s frame. If the CAPWAP packet has NO ieee80211 frame dissected BEFORE this element in the same iteration (so no fresh p_add), then p_isDMG points to the `isDMG` of a dissect_ieee80211_common invocation from a PREVIOUS fuzz iteration → **stack-use-after-return read**.

BUT WAIT — within a SINGLE packet, we can also arrange it: CAPWAP data message with ieee80211 frames is dissected... hmm, order matters: if ieee80211 frames come AFTER the IEEE80211_INFORMATION_ELEMENT in the same packet, the very first packet processed would have no proto data at all (p_isDMG==NULL → fine). We need TWO packets OR one packet where the IE element comes before any ieee80211 frame AND... but if there's NO previous packet, p_get returns NULL → `isDMG = FALSE` — no crash.

So we NEED the stale pointer from a previous packet: The fuzzer harness (LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput) — does it dissect the input TWICE? or does the wmem file scope persist across iterations? libFuzzer runs the same file ONCE for a single input file run... but the harness might dissect multiple packets per input? No — one input = one packet.

Hmm! But libFuzzer, when running normally (not -runs=1), executes LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput MANY times (mutations). BUT the ARVO crash reproduction typically runs the fuzzer binary once with the single input file — libFuzzer will run it... once? Actually libFuzzer with a file argument runs each file once? By default, libFuzzer runs each input file ONCE ("Running 1 inputs 1 time(s) each").

So the crash must occur within ONE iteration. Therefore we need, within ONE packet dissection:
1. Something calls dissect_ieee80211_common (storing &isDMG of THAT invocation in file-scope proto data), 
2. dissect_ieee80211_common RETURNS,
3. Then add_tagged_field is called directly (capwap path) → reads the dead frame.

FUZZ_DISSECTORS="ip"
FUZZ_IP_PROTO_DISSECTORS="udp ospf"
FUZZ_TCP_PORT_DISSECTORS="bgp"
FUZZ_UDP_PORT_DISSECTORS="dns bootp"
FUZZ_MEDIA_TYPE_DISSECTORS="json"
generate_fuzzer()
{
  local fuzzer_target="$1" fuzzer_cflags="$2" fuzzer_name
  fuzzer_name="fuzzshark_$1"
  $CC $CFLAGS -I $SRC/wireshark/ `pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0`       $SRC/wireshark/tools/oss-fuzzshark.c       -c -o $WORK/${fuzzer_name}.o       $fuzzer_cflags
  $CXX $CXXFLAGS $WORK/${fuzzer_name}.o       -o $OUT/${fuzzer_name}       ${WIRESHARK_FUZZERS_COMMON_FLAGS}
  echo -en "[libfuzzer]\nmax_len = 1024\n" > $OUT/${fuzzer_name}.options
  if [ -d "$SAMPLES_DIR/${fuzzer_target}" ]; then
    zip -j $OUT/${fuzzer_name}_seed_corpus.zip $SAMPLES_DIR/${fuzzer_target}/*/*.bin
  fi
}
export WIRESHARK_INSTALL_PATH="$WORK/install"
mkdir -p "$WIRESHARK_INSTALL_PATH"
SAMPLES_DIR="$WORK/samples"
mkdir -p "$SAMPLES_DIR"
cp -a $SRC/wireshark-fuzzdb/samples/* "$SAMPLES_DIR"
CONFOPTS="--disable-shared --enable-static --without-plugins"
CONFOPTS="$CONFOPTS --without-pcap --without-ssl --without-gnutls"
CONFOPTS="$CONFOPTS --disable-wireshark --disable-tshark --disable-sharkd              --disable-dumpcap --disable-capinfos --disable-captype --disable-randpkt --disable-dftest              --disable-editcap --disable-mergecap --disable-reordercap --disable-text2pcap              --without-extcap          "
sed -i '/AC_WIRESHARK_GCC_FORTIFY_SOURCE_CHECK/d' configure.ac
./autogen.sh
./configure --prefix="$WIRESHARK_INSTALL_PATH" $CONFOPTS --disable-warnings-as-errors
make "-j$(nproc)"
make install
WIRESHARK_FUZZERS_COMMON_FLAGS="-lFuzzingEngine     -L"$WIRESHARK_INSTALL_PATH/lib" -lwireshark -lwiretap -lwsutil     -Wl,-Bstatic `pkg-config --libs glib-2.0` -pthread -lpcre -lgcrypt -lgpg-error -lz -Wl,-Bdynamic"
for dissector in $FUZZ_DISSECTORS; do
  generate_fuzzer "${dissector}" -DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TARGET=\"$dissector\"
done
for dissector in $FUZZ_IP_PROTO_DISSECTORS; do
  generate_fuzzer "ip_proto-${dissector}" "-DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TABLE=\"ip.proto\" -DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TARGET=\"$dissector\""
done
for dissector in $FUZZ_TCP_PORT_DISSECTORS; do
  generate_fuzzer "tcp_port-${dissector}" "-DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TABLE=\"tcp.port\" -DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TARGET=\"$dissector\""
done
for dissector in $FUZZ_UDP_PORT_DISSECTORS; do
  generate_fuzzer "udp_port-${dissector}" "-DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TABLE=\"udp.port\" -DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TARGET=\"$dissector\""
done
for dissector in $FUZZ_MEDIA_TYPE_DISSECTORS; do
  generate_fuzzer "media_type-${dissector}" "-DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TABLE=\"media_type\" -DFUZZ_DISSECTOR_TARGET=\"$dissector\""
done

Submit with `bash ./submit.sh PATH_TO_POC` (POSTs to http://172.31.77.1:8666/submit-vul, metadata task_id=arvo:1268, checksum=14f62b36cd4ed...). User directive: work autonomously, never ask for human response, finish when solved.

COMPLETED:
- Extracted repo-vul.tar.gz → /workspace/src-vul/wireshark (snapshot ≈ mid-July 2016: ChangeLog top commit d5f84c0 "Build 2.1.1" Jul 14 2016; config.h PACKAGE_VERSION 2.3.0; prebuilt .o files present)
- Read description.txt ("stack-use-after-return vulnerability in ieee80211 code"); analyzed build.sh (targets: FUZZ_DISSECTORS="ip"; ip.proto udp,ospf; tcp bgp; udp dns,bootp; json — no direct ieee80211 target) and oss-fuzzshark.c harness (pkt_encap=G_MAXINT16, fuzz dissector as POSTDISSECTOR on whole raw buffer, max_len=1024)
- Identified ieee80211 entry points from targets: packet-capwap.c L3375 (udp.port 5246/5247 → ieee80211 "wlan_withoutfcs") and packet-wassp.c L809
- **Ruled out AirPDCAP as SUAR source**: AIRPDCAP_CONTEXT (airpdcap_system.h L155-166) stores keys BY VALUE (memcpy into ctx->keys); sa->key points into global ctx->keys array; used_key copied out via memcpy(key, sa->key, sizeof(AIRPDCAP_KEY_ITEM)) in AirPDcapWepMng; no stack pointer escapes into global ctx
- **Ruled out other stack-escape candidates**: whdr → static whdrs[4] (tap safe); out_buff[SHORT_STR]/iv_buff[4]/dec_data[AIRPDCAP_MAX_CAPLEN] used only within their functions; decrypted payload copied via wmem_memdup(pinfo->pool,...)
- **FOUND prime SUAR candidate**: packet-ieee80211.c L17172 in dissect_ieee80211_common(): `p_add_proto_data(wmem_file_scope(), pinfo, proto_wlan, IS_DMG_KEY, &isDMG)` — stores address of STACK local `isDMG` into FILE-SCOPED proto data (persists across packets/iterations); read back at L14339 in `add_tagged_field()`: `gboolean *p_isDMG = p_get_proto_data(wmem_file_scope(), ...); isDMG = p_isDMG ? *p_isDMG : FALSE;` → copied into `field_data.isDMG`
- add_tagged_field (L14327, non-static/exported) callers found in-file: L11935, L12078, L12502, L12578 (nested IE dissectors via field_data), L16782
- Web search for fix commit FAILED (ERR_PROXY_CONNECTION_FAILED, browser unusable) — offline analysis only

PENDING:
- Inspect packet-ieee80211.c L17122-17190: is the p_add_proto_data call conditional (e.g., `if (tree)`), where is `isDMG` set/used — determines how a stale pointer survives
- Check harness lifetime semantics: does oss-fuzzshark.c build a proto tree (tree NULL vs non-NULL)? Is init_dissection called once (file scope persists across iterations) or per iteration? (If file scope freed per iteration, stale pointer = freed-heap read, not SUAR)
- Grep tree-wide for callers of exported `add_tagged_field` — a path reaching it WITHOUT dissect_ieee80211_common's p_add in the same iteration (or with common early-returning before L17172) = trigger
- Check IS_CTRL_GRANT_OR_GRANT_ACK_KEY proto-data usage (second potential stack-address escape)

Postdissectors in Wireshark receive pinfo — the SAME pinfo! — and they run AFTER the frame dissector. In our harness, the frame dissector is "data" (encap unknown). **What about the ORDER: udp → capwap control (elements: IE → add_tagged_field) — and the same udp packet ALSO being dissected by the udp dissector TWICE? BUT — **AH HA — LOOK AT THIS: `if (pinfo->fd->flags.visited) { udp_p_info = p_get_proto_data(wmem_file_scope(), pinfo, hfi_udp->id, pinfo->curr_layer_num); if (udp_p_info) { call_heur_dissector_direct(...); return; } }`** — this is the "visited" fast path. When dissecting the SAME packet TWICE (visited set after first dissection), UDP reads file-scope proto data keyed by hfi_udp->id + curr_layer_num! And udp_p_info->heur_dtbl_entry — a POINTER TO A HEUR_DISFACTORY_ENTRY (static, fine) — hmm, but this only applies to heuristic matches.

Interesting but not our bug.

**NOW THE CRITICAL INSIGHT — I need to re-examine WHO calls add_tagged_field AFTER a common.** Let me enumerate ALL call chains again very carefully by looking at where dissect_ieee80211_mgt is called (18831, in common) — fine. 

Hmm — hold on, WAIT. Let me reconsider the problem completely. What if the stale pointer is read in a LATER, DEEPER-NESTED common?! No — common re-p_adds at entry.

**WHAT IF p_add_proto_data THROWS or... no.

Hmm, what about **ieee80211_mgt being invoked NOT from common** — dissect_ieee80211_mgt called only from 18831 (common). OK.

**What about ieee80211_dissect... hmm.

**COMPLETELY DIFFERENT: What about the SECOND packet in a SINGLE udp dissection — via UDP reassembly!!** udp has reassembly: dissect_udp: if udp_reassembly && fragmented → fragment_add → process_reassembled_data → if reassembled, the udp dissector dissects the REASSEMBLED udp datagram (decode_udp_ports on it) — still ONE decode_udp_ports.

**What about IP fragmentation in the "ip" binary?** dissect_ip → fragmented → reassembled → the ip dissector calls the ip.proto dissector on the reassembled data (udp) → udp → capwap. ONE udp.

Hmm — so, to reiterate the only remaining scenario: **the SAME udp packet triggers capwap_control's IE add_tagged_field with a stale pointer stored by a PREVIOUS ieee80211 dissection — and the previous ieee80211 dissection happened in THE SAME libFuzzer run via... hmm...

WAIT!!! — **What if ieee80211 is dissected on the udp payload via... "udp.dissector"... NO. BUT — WHAT ABOUT **UDP HEURISTIC DISSECTORS**?! Is ieee80211 a HEURISTIC udp dissector? Hmm — no.

**WHAT ABOUT CAPWAP ITSELF BEING REACHED VIA HEURISTIC + PORT?** — no.

Hmm — hold on. Let me look at the udp dissector (dissect_udp) around line 1131 — maybe it calls decode_udp_ports TWICE (for udp over udp?) or for "udp.check..." hmm. Actually — what about the UDP dissector with **UDP reassembly**: dissect_udp → if udp is fragmented (first fragment...) → fragment_add → not complete → "call_data_dissector"... then when the LAST fragment arrives (SAME udp packet? no — one packet)...

OK — time for a totally different strategy: **BUILD THE FUZZER LOCALLY AND EXPERIMENT.** The prebuilt .o files — are they ASAN-instrumented? Earlier nm grep found "__asan" 26 matches in packet-ieee80211.o — hmm, that's a lot; maybe they ARE instrumented! If I can link fuzzshark_udp_port-... — WAIT, which binary? The ARVO arvo:1268 — the vulnerable BUILD's fuzzer — hmm, the PoC will be tested against the specific fuzzer used in the OSS-Fuzz report. The description says ieee80211; the crash report would name the fuzz target. Common guess: fuzzshark_ip_proto-udp? or fuzzshark_udp_port-dns? Hmm.

Hmm — wait, let me reconsider the target question. To reach capwap or ieee80211, the fuzz dissector must dispatch into udp. The candidates that do that: "ip" (ip→udp), "ip_proto-udp" (ip.proto=17→udp), "udp_port-*" (udp.port=dns/bootp — these binaries dissect input as udp?? I am thinking...: No UDP-over-UDP re-dissection. One decode_udp_ports per udp dissection.

I've been stuck on the in-packet ordering. Let me now seriously evaluate the **two-execution hypothesis** more concretely — is the SAME input really executed twice by libFuzzer? `TryDetectingAMemoryLeak` runs the callback AGAIN only if HasMoreMallocsThanFrees. Wireshark dissecting a packet: allocates via g_malloc/wmem — the packet pool IS reused/freed (wmem_packet_scope freed per iteration? hmm — actually epan_dissect_reset does dissect_cleanup → wmem_free_all(packet pool)?). File scope allocs persist. If net allocs > frees in an iteration, the leak check re-runs the callback (with lsan disabled) — the re-run happens ONLY ONCE more (and then it checks lsan for the second run). So the SAME input executes up to 2x. That's a REAL cross-iteration channel!

For the crash on the 2nd execution, the 2nd dissection must differ from the 1st in a way that avoids re-entering common before add_tagged_field... same bytes → same code path... UNLESS some file-scope state changes the path:

**CAPWAP REASSEMBLY!!!** — THIS IS THE KEY, I think:
- Execution 1: CAPWAP **control** packet, F=1 (fragment), L=0 (more=TRUE → not last), frag_id=X, frag_offset=0 → fragment_add_check → stored, NOT complete → `next_tvb == NULL` → `call_data_dissector(next_tvb...)` → the CAPWAP control header/elements are NEVER dissected in execution 1!! The fragment payload sits in the reassembly table (file-scope/global).
- Execution 2: SAME packet: F=1, L=0 again → fragment_add_check again with same id/offset... hmm — would it consider complete? The head now has fragment[0]=len N more=TRUE from exec 1, and exec 2 adds fragment[0] again... `fragment_add_work`: for a fragment with same offset... hmm — it might APPEND another fragment with the same offset, or... Actually — **hmm, will fragment_add_check REMOVE the previous? Let me think... fd_head → if (frag_offset == 0 && !more) → complete... more=TRUE → not complete. The fragments list gets a second entry with same offset — reassembly still incomplete (hole at the end). So exec 2 also not dissected. ✗.

- **F=1, L=1 (last)**: exec 1: fragment at offset 0, more=FALSE, len = payload len → fragment_add_check → COMPLETE immediately → reassembled → dissect_capwap_control_header + dissect_capwap_message_element on the reassembled tvb → IE(1029) → add_tagged_field with p_isDMG = ... NULL in exec 1 (no ieee80211 dissection before) → safe. exec 2: same → reassembles again (does fragment_add_check RESET the entry after completion? — fragment_add_check: after reassembly completes... I believe when a fragment completes reassembly, the head is marked... the table entry is removed (fragment_free_key?) hmm — process_reassembled_data → "show_reassembly_data"... then the fd_head is freed via fragment_delete? I THINK after successful reassembly, the entry is deleted, so exec 2 repeats the same behavior. ✗ same path.

Hmm — so reassembly doesn't create the asymmetry.

**What about `pinfo->fd->flags.visited`?** — fd is re-initialized per iteration (frame_data_init) → visited=0 each run. ✗.

**What about UDP "visited" path?** fd fresh → visited 0. ✗.

**What about the conversation (udp conversation)?** persists across runs (epan session). Any dissector whose behavior depends on conversation data? CAPWAP? no. UDP: udpd->stream — no path change.

**What about ieee80211 file-scope state: `wlan_stats`? static, zeroed. `whdrs` static — reused. **`ieee80211_l? hmm.

Hmm — what about **wmem_file_scope proto data for UDP (udp_p_info)**: only stored on heuristic match. The udp.port match doesn't store.

OK — so with the same input run twice and NO path asymmetry, the cross-run scenario gives: exec1 common(p_add &isDMG_E1)→return; exec2 common(p_add &isDMG_E2 — overwrites; then reads &isDMG_E2 — valid). No crash. ✗✗.

**THEREFORE the crash MUST happen within ONE execution.** Let me think REALLY hard about in-execution ordering once more...

In-execution ordering candidates:
(A) capwap control: element1=ieee80211 frame? NO such element... **WAIT — ACTUALLY — hold on — what about the control channel DTLS (preamble type 1) → dtls → ... no.

(B) capwap data T=1 wbid=1 → ieee80211 frame (common: p_add; common dissects; common RETURNS) → back in dissect_capwap_data → ... returns → udp done. ✗.

(C) capwap data K=1 → keepalive elements → IE(1029) → add_tagged_field (p_isDMG — needs prior common IN SAME execution — none before in this packet if this is the first ieee80211-ish thing... unless a PREVIOUS run's common left the stale pointer!! ✗ same-execution requirement... hmm — BUT WAIT — hold on — with the two-execution leak-check re-run: exec1 = keepalive IE(1029) → add_tagged_field with p_isDMG=NULL (safe). exec2 = same → NULL → p_get returns... hmm, p_get on a key that was never SET in exec1? It WAS set... in exec1 p_add never happened (no common) → NULL → safe. ✗.

(D) **wassp**: TLVs: ieee80211 TLV (common → maybe THROWS → CATCH_NONFATAL continues) → more TLVs... but no add_tagged_field in wassp. ✗.

(E) **capwap data T=1 wbid=1 ieee80211 frame → ieee80211 → common → common THROWS mid-way (after p_add) → exception propagates through dissect_capwap_data (no TRY!) → udp (no TRY) → postdissector TRY in dissect_frame → CATCH_BOUNDS... show_exception → dissect_frame continues → ... tap_queue_packet, frame_end_routines, colorize... → dissect_record returns → epan_dissect_reset → LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput returns. Then the leak-detect re-run (exec 2): same input → same throw. ✗.

(F) **ieee80211 → dissect_ieee80211_data → ieee8023/LLC → ip → udp → capwap?!?!** — WAIT: ieee80211 DATA frames can carry LLC/802.2 → ip! And ieee80211 dissects "ieee80211_data" → ethertype → call_subdissector... If an ieee80211 DATA frame contains an LLC/IP/UDP packet with dst port 5246 → capwap CONTROL → control elements → IE(1029) → add_tagged_field — AND the ieee80211 common IS STILL ON THE STACK (we're inside common's call chain!) — VALID pointer — NO CRASH. ✗ (but interesting for nesting!).

(G) **REVERSE NESTING!!! CAPWAP data (5247) → ieee80211 frame → ... common → returns → capwap_data returns → udp... hmm ✗.

WAIT — (F) gives nesting; can we get the REVERSE: add_tagged_field called INSIDE, while an OUTER common has RETURNED? Sequence: capwap data T=1 wbid=1 → ieee80211 frame A → common(p_add &isDMG_A) → common RETURNS. Then capwap... hmm ✗ capwap_data can't continue.

Hmm — what about **ieee80211 frame A → data → LLC → 802.3 → ip → udp → capwap CONTROL → IE(1029) (add_tagged_field — VALID &isDMG_A — inside common A!) → control ALSO parses ieee80211 element?? no...

Hmm — (F) is: common A on stack; add_tagged_field inside — reads &isDMG_A — VALID.
